items.title: Constitutional posts & key appointments (2025-26)
items.body:
## Who holds what (2026)

| Post | Incumbent | Since |
|---|---|---|
| President | Droupadi Murmu | 25 Jul 2022 |
| Vice-President | C. P. Radhakrishnan | 12 Sep 2025 |
| Prime Minister | Narendra Modi | 26 May 2014 |
| Chief Justice of India (53rd) | Surya Kant | 24 Nov 2025 |
| Lok Sabha Speaker | Om Birla | 19 Jun 2019 |
| Chief Election Commissioner | Gyanesh Kumar | 19 Feb 2025 |
| RBI Governor (26th) | Sanjay Malhotra | 11 Dec 2024 |

## Points to note

- **C. P. Radhakrishnan** became the 15th Vice-President after **Jagdeep Dhankhar** resigned; the VP is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64).
- **Surya Kant** is the 53rd CJI; recent order was Chandrachud (50th) - Sanjiv Khanna (51st) - B. R. Gavai (52nd) - Surya Kant (53rd).
- **Gyanesh Kumar** is CEC under the new selection framework (CEC & other ECs Act, 2023).
keyPoints: President = Droupadi Murmu (since 25 Jul 2022, 15th President).
Vice-President = C. P. Radhakrishnan (since 12 Sep 2025), ex-officio Rajya Sabha Chairman.
Surya Kant is the 53rd CJI, sworn in 24 Nov 2025, succeeding B. R. Gavai.
Gyanesh Kumar is Chief Election Commissioner since 19 Feb 2025.
Sanjay Malhotra is the 26th RBI Governor since 11 Dec 2024 (after Shaktikanta Das).
items.source: Wikipedia — 2026 in India / Chief Justice of India; Weekly CA PDFs (Nov 2025)

items.title: Economic Survey 2025-26 & Union Budget 2026-27
items.body:
## Economic Survey 2025-26

- Tabled in Parliament by the **Finance Minister** ahead of the Budget; prepared by the **Economic Division, DEA** under the **Chief Economic Adviser (CEA)**.
- **Real GDP growth (FY26): 7.4%**; GVA growth 7.3%; **FY27 outlook 6.8-7.2%** — keeping India the fastest-growing major economy.
- Theme: India moving from **"Strategic Resilience" to "Strategic Indispensability"**.
- Private Final Consumption ~61.5% of GDP (highest since 2012); GFCF up 7.8%.
- The Survey was **integrated with the Budget in 1950-51** and became a **separate document in 1964**.

## Union Budget 2026-27

- Presented by FM **Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2026** (Annual Financial Statement, Article 112).
- The new **Income Tax Act, 2025** replaced the six-decade-old Income-tax Act, 1961, taking effect **1 April 2026**.
keyPoints: Economic Survey 2025-26: real GDP growth FY26 = 7.4%, FY27 outlook 6.8-7.2%.
Survey theme: 'Strategic Resilience' to 'Strategic Indispensability'; prepared under the CEA.
Economic Survey became a separate document (from the Budget) in 1964.
Union Budget 2026-27 presented by Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 Feb 2026.
Income Tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act, effective 1 April 2026.
items.source: Weekly CA PDF — January Week 4 (Economic Survey 2025-26); PIB — Union Budget 2026-27

items.title: Key schemes, bills & laws (2025-26)
items.body:
## VB-G RAM G Bill (to replace MGNREGA)

- Full name: **Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)**.
- Proposes to replace **MGNREGA**, raising the wage-employment guarantee from **100 to 125 days**.
- Mandates wage payment within **7-15 days**, with allowances for delay; focus on durable rural assets.

## Central Excise (Amendment) Bill, 2025

- Raised **excise duty on tobacco products** — revenue plus public-health objective.
- Central excise now largely applies to items outside GST (tobacco, petroleum).

## National Dental Commission (March 2026)

- Replaced the **Dental Council of India** (Dentists Act, 1948) to modernise dental education/regulation — mirroring the NMC reform of 2020.
keyPoints: VB-G RAM G = Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin); replaces MGNREGA.
VB-G RAM G raises the employment guarantee to 125 days (from MGNREGA's 100).
Central Excise (Amendment) Bill 2025 raised duties on tobacco products.
National Dental Commission (Mar 2026) replaced the Dental Council of India.
items.source: Weekly CA PDFs — December Week 3 (VB-G RAM G), December Week 1 (Excise); Wikipedia — 2026 in India (NDC)

items.title: Padma Awards 2026 & civilian honours
items.body:
## Padma Awards 2026

- **131 awards** approved: **5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan, 113 Padma Shri**; 19 women, 16 posthumous, 6 foreigners/NRI/PIO/OCI.
- **Padma Vibhushan (5):** Dharmendra Deol (Art, posthumous), K. T. Thomas (Public Affairs), N. Rajam (Art — violinist), P. Narayanan (Literature & Education), V. S. Achuthanandan (Public Affairs, posthumous — former Kerala CM).
- **Padma Bhushan (notable):** Alka Yagnik, Mammootty, Uday Kotak, Vijay Amritraj, Bhagat Singh Koshyari; Piyush Pandey and Shibu Soren (posthumous).

## Order of civilian honours

- **Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.**
- No new **Bharat Ratna** was conferred during Nov 2025-Oct 2026.
- The 'Bharat Ratna Dr. Bhupen Hazarika National Awards' (Nov 2025, Guwahati) are separate cultural awards named after Hazarika, not the Bharat Ratna itself.
keyPoints: Padma Awards 2026 total = 131 (5 Vibhushan, 13 Bhushan, 113 Shri).
2026 Padma Vibhushan: Dharmendra, K.T. Thomas, N. Rajam, P. Narayanan, V.S. Achuthanandan.
Uday Kotak, Alka Yagnik, Mammootty, Vijay Amritraj received the Padma Bhushan 2026.
Civilian honours order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.
No new Bharat Ratna was announced in the Nov 2025-Oct 2026 window.
items.source: Weekly CA PDF — January Week 4 (Padma Awards 2026); November Week I

| Index / Report | Publisher | India's rank |

| Climate Change Performance Index 2026 | Germanwatch et al. | 23rd (from 10th) |
| Henley Passport Index 2026 | Henley & Partners | 80th (~55 destinations) |

| Milk production | — | 1st (~247.87 MT) |

## Points to note

- **CCPI** always leaves the **top 3 ranks vacant** (no country fully Paris-aligned).
- **Asia Power Index** order: US (1st) > China (2nd) > **India (3rd)** > Japan (4th).
- In the **AI Vibrancy Index** India is behind only the USA and China.
keyPoints: CCPI 2026: India 23rd (slipped from 10th); top 3 ranks always left vacant.
Henley Passport Index 2026: India 80th.
Asia Power Index 2025 (Lowy): India 3rd, upgraded to a 'major power'.
Global AI Vibrancy Index 2025: India 3rd, behind USA and China.

items.title: Defence & space milestones (2025-26)
items.body:
## Navy commissionings

- **INS Mahe** — lead ship of the **Mahe-class anti-submarine warfare shallow water craft (ASW-SWC)** for coastal sub-hunting.
- **INS Aridaman** — India's **third indigenous SSBN** (nuclear-powered ballistic-missile submarine), after Arihant and Arighaat, under the ATV programme; strengthens the sea leg of the nuclear triad.

## Missiles & space

- **DRDO LRLACM** (Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile) flight-tested from **Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha** — subsonic precision deep-strike, ground- and ship-launchable.
- **ISRO:** the **first PSLV built by Indian industry** (under ISRO supervision) targeted an early-2026 launch — a step toward privatised launch vehicles.
- **NISAR** — the joint **NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar** earth-observation satellite; **Gaganyaan** (crewed) remains ISRO's flagship goal.
keyPoints: INS Mahe = lead ship of the Mahe-class ASW shallow water craft.
INS Aridaman = India's third indigenous SSBN (nuclear ballistic-missile submarine).
DRDO's LRLACM is a Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile, tested from Abdul Kalam Island.
First industry-built PSLV (under ISRO) targeted an early-2026 launch.
NISAR is a joint NASA-ISRO earth-observation (SAR) satellite.
items.source: Weekly CA PDFs — November Week 3 (INS Mahe/PSLV), December Week 1 (INS Aridaman); Wikipedia — 2026 in India (LRLACM)

items.title: Summits, trade, sports, infrastructure & elections (2026)
items.body:
## Summits & trade

- **AI Impact Summit** hosted in **New Delhi (February 2026)** — India as a hub for inclusive, development-focused AI.
- **India-EU FTA** politically concluded in early 2026; **New Zealand-India FTA** signed in New Delhi (April 2026).

## Sports

- **2026 Men's T20 World Cup** (cricket) co-hosted by **India and Sri Lanka** (Feb-Mar 2026).
- India awarded hosting rights for the **2028 World Athletics Indoor Championships** (Bhubaneswar) — the 4th Asian nation to host it.

## Infrastructure & elections

- **Noida International Airport (Jewar, UP)** inaugurated by PM Modi on **28 March 2026**.
- **Assembly elections (Apr-May 2026):** Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry; the ECI conducted a **Special Intensive Revision (SIR)** of electoral rolls, whose validity the Supreme Court examined.
keyPoints: India hosted the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi (Feb 2026).
India-EU FTA concluded and NZ-India FTA signed in New Delhi in 2026.
2026 Men's T20 World Cup co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka.
Noida International Airport (Jewar, UP) inaugurated on 28 Mar 2026.
2026 Assembly polls: Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Puducherry; ECI ran a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of rolls.

items.title: Exam-Precision: Labour Codes, MSME, Piprahwa, NTDs, CETA & BRICS 2026
items.body:
## Laws & economy

- **Four labour codes** (Wages; Industrial Relations; Social Security; Occupational Safety, Health & Working Conditions) came into force **nationally on 21 November 2025**, consolidating 29 central labour laws.
- **MSME revised classification** with **enhanced investment/turnover limits** took effect **1 April 2025** (announced in Budget 2025-26).

## Heritage & health

- The **Piprahwa relics** (associated with the Buddha) were first discovered in **1898 by William Claxton Peppe** at a site identified with ancient **Kapilavastu**; the reliquary inscription is in the **Brahmi** script (not Kharosthi).
- By early 2026, **58 countries** had eliminated **at least one Neglected Tropical Disease (NTD)** per the WHO.

## Trade & diplomacy

- **India-UK CETA** (Comprehensive Economic & Trade Agreement) was a major bilateral trade milestone of 2025-26.
- **India assumed the BRICS chairship on 1 January 2026** and hosts the **18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi**.
keyPoints: The four labour codes came into force nationally on 21 November 2025.
MSME enhanced investment/turnover limits took effect on 1 April 2025.
Piprahwa relics were discovered in 1898 by W.C. Peppe near Kapilavastu; the inscription is in Brahmi script.
By early 2026, 58 countries had eliminated at least one Neglected Tropical Disease (WHO).
India-UK CETA was a landmark 2025-26 trade agreement.
India took the BRICS chair on 1 January 2026 and hosts the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
items.source: PIB; WHO; Ministry of Labour; reputable 2025-26 CA compilations (verified Sep 2026)

items.title: National current-affairs timeline — recent additions (Sep 2025 & Sep 2026)
items.body:
A month-wise recap of national developments added to this bank for the thin Sep 2025 and Sep 2026 windows. Current affairs in this app are updated through **9 October 2026**.

| Date | Development |
|---|---|
| 3 Sep 2025 | GST reforms (“GST 2.0”) — rates reduced/rationalised on many goods. |
| 9/12 Sep 2025 | C. P. Radhakrishnan elected 15th Vice-President (early poll after Dhankhar’s resignation). |
| 13 Sep 2025 | PM Modi’s first Manipur visit since the May 2023 violence. |
| 15 Sep 2025 | Supreme Court stays parts of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025. |
| 26 Sep 2025 | IAF formally retires the MiG-21 fleet after ~62 years. |
| 27 Sep 2025 | Cold Desert (Himachal) designated a UNESCO biosphere reserve. |
| 12-13 Sep 2026 | 18th BRICS Summit, New Delhi — New Delhi Declaration adopted. |
keyPoints: GST 2.0 reforms announced 3 Sep 2025 (rate rationalisation).
C. P. Radhakrishnan — 15th Vice-President (oath 12 Sep 2025).
SC stayed parts of Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025 on 15 Sep 2025.
IAF retired MiG-21 on 26 Sep 2025 after ~62 years.
